source_refs.note: Topic printed 3.7.2.2 Binary Search (PDF 85-86, printed 82-83); Figure 3.7 is replaced by the original diagram with the same list. The example omits the target number; 7 is inferred from 'finds the target immediately'. Long question 3 is answered. Recorded.

blocks.text: Binary Search is an efficient algorithm for finding an item in a sorted list. It works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half and discarding the half where the item cannot be, until the item is found or the interval is empty.

items: Start with the middle element of the sorted list.
If the middle element is the target, return its position.
If the target is smaller than the middle element, repeat the search on the left half.
If the target is larger, repeat the search on the right half.

blocks.text: Example: Suppose you have a sorted list [1,3,5,7,9,11,13] and you are searching for the number

items: Binary Search will start at the middle element (7) and find the target immediately.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book leaves out the number being searched for. Since Binary Search finds the target immediately at the middle element (7), the number searched for is 7.

Complexity: The time complexity of Binary Search is O(log n), making it much faster than linear search algorithms, especially for large datasets. Figure 3.7 illustrates the binary search process, showing how the search interval is halved at each step, making the search more efficient.

blocks.alt: BINARY SEARCH: five copies of the sorted list 21, 34, 43, 57, 66, 78 with step notes. Search 78, divide from the middle and check mid (43); 78 > 43, look for 78 in the right half; new mid = 66, check mid; 78 > 66, look on the right half; new mid = 78, element found at mid (circled).
blocks.caption: Figure 3.7: Binary Search Process (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.7).

blocks.title: Did You Know?
blocks.text: Binary Search is only effective on sorted lists. If your data isn't sorted, consider using a sorting algorithm like Merge Sort before applying Binary Search!
